messages:
frank (eng-security): FYI: runc CVE-2026-0420 landed in upstream. it permits a local container process to escalate on older kernels. we need a coordinated base-image rebuild, KMS signing check, and an audit backfill for some elevated build-service actions last Wednesday.

aya (eng-runtime): thanks. prefer we do a staged push: staging only -> runtime fuzz + smoke -> 1% canary -> full. can infra gate registry pushes?

ben (eng-infra): yes. i'll create a short maintenance window and a registry-policy 'staging-only' flag. also will freeze the builder pool during cut. need to know signer identity for ACLs.

sofia (sec): current signer: serviceAccount:build-signer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com. note: last week ops briefly granted iam.serviceAccounts.actAs to build-service to unblock a deploy. i'll run an audit query to capture any sign/push activity during that interval. i'll also prefer using a short-lived wrapped key for the rebuild job rather than restoring long-lived perms.

frank (eng-security): proposed checklist:
1) issue ephemeral wrapped key for pipeline
2) rebuild base images (debian-14) with patched runc + Dockerfile hardening (no_new_privs, drop caps)
3) cosign sign with KMS-wrapped key and emit structured audit events
4) run SCA + SBOM diff and runtime fuzz in staging
5) canary 1% with auto-rollback on kernel oops

ci-bot: ci: rebuild queued: id=rbld-17670-stg initiator=frank. watch: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/rbld-17670-stg

aya (eng-runtime): runtime tests to run after staging image is pushed:
- kubectl run runc-smoke --image=registry.staging.redwood/base:patched --restart=Never --overrides='{"spec": {"containers": [{"securityContext": {"allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}}]}}'
- start runtime-fuzzer (30m) against canary pods
- enable core-dump collection and automatic rollback on kernel panic

ben (eng-infra): infra notes:
- cosign via KMS plugin: cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/build/cryptoKeys/wrap
- pipeline must emit JSON audit for build:start, build:push, image:sign, key:wrap
- registry: implement quick-revoke endpoint POST /v1/revoke {"image":"..."}

sofia (sec): audit query i'll run for backfill:
logName="projects/redwood/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"build-service@redwood"
protoPayload.methodName:("google.iam.admin.v1.SetIamPolicy" OR "google.iam.admin.v1.BindRole" OR "google.cloud.kms.v1.CryptoKeyVersion.AsymmetricSign")
timestamp>="2026-03-05T00:00:00Z" AND timestamp<"2026-03-07T00:00:00Z"
correlate with gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-17670-stg/* and KMS audit for keyRing 'build'.

frank (eng-security): if we find artifacts signed by the old principal in that window, mark them untrusted and trigger rbld-quick-resign plan. document everything in incident-runbook.

ci-bot: job rbld-17670-stg completed: status=SUCCESS duration=14m artifacts at gs://redwood-build-logs/rbld-17670-stg/

sofia (sec): kicking audit backfill now. i'll paste correlated CSV shortly. preliminary scan: no unexpected sign operations in that window.

aya (eng-runtime): staging canary up. added eBPF probe for prctl & ptrace and increased OOM/kern oops alert sensitivity for the canary group.

ben (eng-infra): registry staging-only flag set. quick-revoke endpoint deployed in case we need emergency untrust.

sofia (sec): audit CSV uploaded to ticket. no suspect signer activity. continuing to monitor for RBAC drift.

frank (eng-security): ok owners: ben=infra push & registry flags, aya=runtime tests & canary policy, sofia=KMS + audit correlation, frank=sec lead + runbook. will move to 1% canary in 10m if no issues. thanks all. :lock:
